analysis: The only changed file is landing/src/app/globals.css, a marketing landing page stylesheet. The visible changes are layout only: removal of the .story-section-heading rule, the .closing/.closing-content/.closing-copy layout moving from absolute to grid/flow, and small selector/size tweaks in the closing area. The visible base lines (4898-6247) and head lines (1-1048) contain only CSS rules, font-face URLs pointing at local /fonts/*.woff2 files and /logo.svg. I saw no external url() references, no data exfiltration vectors and no scripting. Nothing touches the provider process, the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), prefix-cache storage (T-041), keys or tokens. The hunk coordinates in the patch excerpt are not fully visible. The head text only covers lines 1-1048, so the changed ranges at head lines 4014-4317 and 5979-5980 are visible only through the truncated patch excerpt. That excerpt is incomplete. Even so, the evident change type is presentation CSS, and the threat model scopes backend, console and landing hosting out. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated and no updates are needed. The remaining risk is only that unseen CSS in the truncated patch could differ from what the excerpt suggests, which is very unlikely to carry security impact. Further review is not needed.
